5 Between the mansions of Virgo and Libra there ascend a great Asp, which is also called the Ophionian Agathodaemon <note>A "Good Spirit" in serpent form; from the Greek *Agathos* (good) and *Daimon* (spirit).</note>, together with a bowl of wine, according to the testimony of Auenar <note>Abraham Ibn Ezra (c. 1089–1167), a celebrated Jewish scholar and astrologer.</note>. However, the Indian astrologers place a large tree in this location, in whose branches a Dog and an Ibis exist. But let us hear the words of the Author:

<note>Hebrew: "And there rises there a large tree, on its branches a dog and a bird called the Rachama."</note>

> *And there ascends there a large tree, in whose branches are a Dog and a Stork, which is also called an Ibis, and is named Rachama by the Hebrews out of Philostorgia <note>Greek for "natural affection" or "parental love," referring to the stork's reputation for caring for its young.</note>.* And this indicates nothing other than the station of the Mercurial Deities. Furthermore, the Egyptians say, according to Auenar, that in this place is positioned a beautiful virgin, remarkable for the length of her hair, holding two ears of grain in her hand; she sits upon a throne and suckles a tiny boy, and nourishes him with the greatest diligence. <margin>The Virgin suckling a boy in the Zodiac according to the opinion of the Egyptians and Hebrews.</margin> Truly, since the words of Auenar are most worthy of consideration, I provide them here:

<note>Hebrew: "And there rises in the first face [decan] a beautiful maiden with long hair, and in her hand are two ears of corn, and she sits upon a throne, and she raises a small child and suckles him and feeds him."</note>

*In the first face,* he says, *of Virgo, there ascends a beautiful Virgin with long hair, and she holds two ears of grain in her hand, and sits upon a seat, and nourishes a boy still tiny, and suckles him, and feeds him.* Albumazar <note>Abu Ma'shar (787–886), a famous Persian astrologer.</note> describes these things much more expressly in his introduction to Astrology, which words Stefflerus cites in the Sphere of Proclus; he discourses thus: *There rises in the first decan <note>A 10-degree segment of a zodiac sign.</note> of Virgo a girl, <margin>* corrupted</margin> called in Arabic *Aderenosa*, that is, a pure Virgin, an immaculate Virgin, graceful in body, beautiful in countenance, modest in habit, with long hair, holding two ears of corn in her hand, residing upon a canopied throne, nourishing and rightly feeding a boy in a place whose name is Hebrew—a boy, I say, named by certain nations Jesus, signifying Issa, whom the Greeks also call Christ.* These are the words of Albumazar. From these things it is clearly evident that our Savior, born of the unstained Virgin, is indicated. Therefore, this Virgin rises feeding JESUS. Let the defiant Hebrews be ashamed here, while they reject the Virgin Mother, when the Gentiles foresaw these things for so many ages and so many centuries before them. But if a <term>Verpus</term> <note>A derogatory Latin term for a circumcised man, used here by Kircher in a polemical context against Jewish skeptics.</note> should say: *They do not say that this Virgin is the mother of that boy, but only that she is rightly feeding him;* let the unhappy man blush, because she who rightly feeds him is none other than the mother. Something similar is read in the European Sibyl: *He shall come leaping over mountains and hills, and reigning in poverty with the silence of ruling, he shall spring forth from the vessel of the Virgin.* There is also placed in this same spot by the Egyptians the figure of a man <term>Taurophoros</term> <note>Greek for "Bull-bearer."</note>, that is, of a taurine figure. Thus Auenar:

# CHAPTER VI. OF THE EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

->There ascends there the form of a man who has a half-figure, and his head is like the head of a bull, and in his hand is a half-idol of a man, naked; and there also ascends there a half-figure, on whose head is a plow-beam with which he plows the earth.<- <note>original Hebrew: "ויעלה שם אדם שיש לו חצי צורת..."</note>

<margin>Attendants of Sagittarius and Capricorn.</margin>
7 Within the latitude of Sagittarius and Capricorn, the Egyptians place toward the South-North a figure of a young goat holding horns; and it is the same figure which we explained above in the sign of Capricorn: then the figure of a flying Hawk; and in the place of the Hawk, the Greeks thereafter substituted a flying Eagle. Furthermore, the Egyptians place in this space a <term>Cynocephalus</term> <note>Dog-headed; from the Greek kyon (dog) and kephale (head)</note>, that is, the body of an Ape with a canine head. ->And there ascends there the body of an ape and its head is like the head of a dog.<- <note>original Hebrew: "ויעלה שם גוף הקוף..."</note>

<margin>Attendants of Aquarius and Pisces.</margin>
8 Within the station of Aquarius and Pisces they place a Hen with her chicks. The <term>Oxyrhynchus</term> <note>A species of sharp-nosed fish sacred in ancient Egypt</note> fish and the figure of the Nile are named by some.

And these are the images which <term>Auenar</term> reports were inserted into the heavens according to the mind of the Egyptians—symbols of hidden actions, which the Greeks then consigned to posterity, adorned and polished by their own fables; these I have thought fit to set down here. Yet someone might rightly ask at this point by what path I have penetrated into such hidden antiquity; therefore, so that this may be clear, I explain the matter. <term>Michael Schatta</term>, an Egyptian Copt and formerly my <term>Amanuensis</term> <note>A literary assistant or scribe</note> in Rome for transcribing Coptic and Arabic works from the Vatican Library, after he had returned to Egypt, was urged by me among other things that if he should find any hieroglyphic inscriptions, he should take care to have them drawn, a certain sum of money having been assigned for this purpose; which he indeed performed. Among other hieroglyphic fragments, therefore, of which mention will be made in their proper place, he also transmitted this Astronomical description of 48 <term>Iconisms</term> <note>Visual representations or diagrams</note>, drawn from the ancient Library of the Monastery of St. Mercurius, and prepared as much as was possible, to fulfill the promise made to me. Since I recognized that this smelled of the lamp of the Ancients <note>A metaphor meaning it showed signs of late-night, diligent study</note> and was conformable to hieroglyphic doctrine, I [judged] it [necessary to present] it in this place as a rare and unseen [gift] to the curious reader—

->SECTION VII. MATHEMATICAL HIEROGLYPHS. CHAPTER VI.<-

I have thought it timely to share this; and although many parts were mutilated and imperfect, through constant study and diligence, those parts which were missing or appeared obscure have been clarified and polished by the file of a Daedalean mind <note>A reference to Daedalus, the mythical craftsman, implying great technical skill and ingenuity</note> from the very fountain of hieroglyphics. A truly remarkable difference shines forth between these spheres and those of the Greeks. The Egyptians placed not the Equator, but the Zodiac as the base, so that the center of each hemisphere represented not the pole of the World, but the pole of the Zodiac. Secondly, the figures sketched with hieroglyphic symbols do not correspond exactly to their physical locations, but for the most part differ; nor should this seem strange to anyone, since the Egyptians attempted to express in that vast face of the firmament not so much the stars, but the **station of the Divinities**, as was said above. For they did not think, as the Greeks did, that the figures of the Gods were composed by a clustering of stars; rather, they called a certain gathering of stars the "station" of such-and-hers deity, whom they believed ruled over that specific place in the heavens. For they did not, like those who came after them, ascribe the effects shining forth in the lower World to the hidden influence of the stars, but to the power and efficacy of the Divinities established in such-and-such a place in heaven, as has been said. And Achilles Tatius <margin>Achilles Tatius</margin> <note>Kircher refers to him as "Statius," a common historical confusion with the Roman poet</note> in his *Introduction* near the end testifies to this same thing. I cite his words: *“In the Egyptian sphere,”* he says, *“there is neither the Dragon, nor the Bear, nor Cepheus <note>original Greek: Ἐν γοῦν τῇ τῶν Αἰγυπτίων σφαίρᾳ, οὔτε ὁ δράκων ἐστὶ νομιζόμενος, ἢ ὀνομαζόμενος, οὔτε ἄρκτοι, οὔτε κηφεύς</note>, but other forms of idols and names assigned to them; just as it is in that of the Chaldeans. But the Greeks gave these names to the stars from famous Heroes for the sake of utility, so that they might be easily recognized.”* They also made the Zodiac wider than the Greeks did; in its Northern hemisphere, the hieroglyphic figures of the 12 signs of the Zodiac are seen expressed according to the invention of the ancient Astronomy of those still unrefined ages. In the Southern hemisphere, you will find the same signs repeated, but abbreviated: from which it becomes entirely clear where the characters of the signs used to this day—which they resemble—originated. Nor should the Reader look here for degrees of declination, or latitude of stars, or similar divisions; since, as I said, that was not the intent of the ancients; rather, they attempted only to express the stations of the Gods through 12 Rhombs, which they called the <term>Dodecatemorion</term> <note>Greek: δωδεκατώριον; a division of the zodiac into twelve equal parts or "twelfth-parts"</note>. I wished to deduce all these things here at length, lest the curious Reader be unaware of the Egyptians' purpose in placing 48 astronomical images upon the sky. Now, to the Rhomb.

Note that the order of the Signs was placed here starting from Aries <note>Astrological symbol: Aries ♈</note>, even though the Egyptian <term>Hieromanthae</term> <note>Priest-prophets or sacred diviners</note> took their beginning from Capricorn; the reason for which we gave in the preceding pages. Hence, it seemed fit to mark them with two different numerical figures to avoid confusion.

# CHAPTER VII 208 OEDIPUS AEGYPTIACUS HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

->*The Arrangement of Astronomical Icons according to the mind of the Egyptians, which Michael Schatta the Egyptian extracted from ancient Egyptian monuments and transmitted to the Author.*<-

The Astrological-hieroglyphic icons assigned to the heavens by the Egyptians are 48 in total, as will be made clear in due time in the interpretation of the Barberini Obelisk; by these icons, they promised such fortune to those born during their ascent or culmination as was expressed by the symbols. For they report, as I have said above, that they arranged certain stations of the Divinities, in which they believed those deities acted with a particular influence upon the lower things committed to their faith and protection; hence they were called by the Egyptians <note>original: "πινσεκη ιτ τεψ ☿"</note> "stations" or "mansions of the Gods," because in them they attended to the things committed to them with watchful care. Twelve principal ones among these they arranged in the obliquity of the Zodiac; the rest they placed partly in the North and partly in the South, as is evident from the two hemispheres attached here, which were transmitted to me by Michael Schatta the Egyptian. And indeed, the Greeks and all posterity eventually embraced this number of 48 icons; although, as is clear from the hemispheres, the Egyptians differ from the Greeks in both position and order, with the Greeks substituting their own Divinities in place of the Egyptian ones, and as if honoring them with this celestial <term>pandemia</term> <note>A gathering or assembly of all the people/gods</note>. And indeed, we have discussed at length in Chapter 3 above the mystical significance of the twelve presidents arranged in the mansions of the twelve signs of the Zodiac; it remains for us to discuss the rest with equal pace, beginning from the Northern hemisphere.

<margin>
Northern
Icons.
Of the Kingdom
of Ammon.
</margin>
Therefore, the first icon of the Kingdom of Ammon, after the twelve <term>Oecodespotas</term> <note>Rulers of the house; the planetary governors of the zodiac signs</note> of the Zodiac, occurs in the region of Ammon, or the district of Aries: the triangle, which the Egyptians call <term>Delta</term>, and in the Coptic language signifies the same as a "three-cornered gate," through which the entrance for the Gods into Egypt lies open. This is nothing other than that lower part of Egypt, as was shown in the first volume of the first Treatise, which the Nile—divided at Memphis by the branching of the river—once established, having grown from the accumulation of Nilotic silt. It was of such great fertility, therefore, that they thought it should not undeservedly be called the home of the immortal Gods and the heaven of the Gods. They call it the "Gate of the Gods" because through it an entrance lies open to an abundance of all good things granted by the liberality and beneficence of the Gods. When the Ibis, a Mercurial animal <note>Associated with the god Thoth/Hermes/Mercury</note>, expresses this with its legs spread apart, it simultaneously indicates under which Divinity's protection the <term>Delta</term> resides. Hence, in that region of the sky hanging over Egypt, they established a similar triangle or <term>Delta</term> composed of three stars; and posterity followed this with the highest worship and veneration as a station of the Mercurial Divinities favoring Egypt, which the Greeks also included among their own asterisms. See what we have recounted in the first volume, pages 8, 9, 10, 11, in the Pamphilian Obelisk book 3, and in various other places.

The II. Icon is marked as the station of Nephta, who, since she has the things of the lower Horizon committed to her faith, undertakes to defend the Nilotic Delta—that is, Egypt, over which she is placed—against all injuries of the nightly cold...

He carries a handled cross <note>The *crux ansata* or Ankh, a symbol of life.</note> to indicate the abundance of his influence.

III. The Iconism <note>A symbolic representation or image.</note> contained in the same district of Ammon is placed as the image of another tutelary Deity, with bent knees; by its very position and the arrangement of the body, it expresses the Deity of Ammon (as we have shown elsewhere), as if it were supplicating Ammon against the IV. Iconism, the Typhonian Dragon (which has established its station around the North Pole and is, as it were, the indicator of the Typhonian Kingdom).

V. The Iconism is placed within the Rhombus <note>A geometric division of the zodiac or celestial map.</note> of Apis, subject to the jurisdiction of the Bull <note>Taurus</note>; it is a Hen with chicks, which the Egyptians worshipped as a Venereal <note>Associated with Venus/love/fertility.</note> Deity of fertility. VI. The Iconism, established within the same Rhombus, contains the image of one sitting on a throne, distinguished by a headdress of grain-ears and bovine horns, carrying a Teraphim <note>A cult image or idol; here likely a specific Egyptian amulet.</note> in one hand and a handled cross in the other; it is the image of Isis, the tutelary Deity of Egypt, the discoverer of grain and of agriculture by means of oxen, as the symbols show. The seat is an indicator of power; the Teraphim is a symbol of the Apis-amulet, and the Cross is a symbol of benign influence, as if she were about to oppose herself to the Typhonian Dragon, which the IV. Iconism displays. See page 185 of the first Volume, where ample mention is made of this image. This Iconism corresponds to the Cassiopeia of the Greeks.

VII. The Iconism, established within the Rhombus of the Twins <note>Gemini</note>, is the image of Anubis, conspicuous for his dog's head, who carries an arrow in one hand and a water-bucket <note>original: "situlam"</note> in the other; these are symbols of the Nilotic Deity and signify the excess of drought and heat, which is tempered by the moderation of Anubis. See the *Pamphilian Obelisk*.

VIII. The Iconism of Pan is an image in human form carrying a young goat, bearing a staff in one hand and a serpent in the other. The goat is a symbol of wanton fertility, as we have proved in the *Pamphilian Obelisk*; the staff is a symbol of power and vigilance; the serpent is a symbol of life. They intimate by this Iconism the care and diligence of the Panic Deity, by which he is driven to defend the things committed to his faith against the imminent Typhonian force, which is, as it were, contrary to the fertility and life of things.

IX. The Iconism within the Rhombus of Hermanubis <note>A syncretic deity combining Hermes and Anubis.</note>, which corresponds to the Cancer, is an image distinguished by a headdress, carrying a musical instrument in its hands, in place of which the Greeks positioned the Lyre. It indicates, however, that by the authority and power granted to it by Hermanubis, it reduces the burning heats—which the Typhonian force brings into this place for the destruction of things—to a harmonic temperament, and undertakes the defense against the hostile force of Typhon.

# THE EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

<margin>CHAPTER VII.</margin> the Egyptians call <term>Agathodaemon</term> <note>original: "Αγαθοδαίμονα"; literally "Good Spirit," often depicted as a winged serpent or protector deity</note>; about which I have written extensively in the *Pamphilian Obelisk*.

**XI.** The *Iconism* <note>A symbolic figure or representation</note> of the Great Bear <note>Ursa Major</note> displays an image which the Arabs call <note>Arabic text: بنات النعش (Banat al-Na'sh)</note> *Benath alnaaghs*, that is, the "Daughters of the Bier," while the Egyptians call it the "Chariot of *Osiris*." For in this twelfth-part <note>zodiacal sign</note>, *Osiris*—that is, the *Nile*—is imagined to be carried over the land of Egypt as if by a chariot through the force of the inundation, which occurs under the sign of <term>Momphthæ</term> <note>A name Kircher uses for a specific Egyptian divine power or zodiacal aspect</note>, in order to animate and fertilize the land alongside his attendant, the Ophionian <term>Agathodaemon</term>. You will find all these things explained more fully in the *Pamphilian Obelisk*, Book 8, on the Hierogram of the Lion, and below in the chapter on the 28 Mansions of the Moon.

**XII.** The *Iconism* placed within the Rhombus of Isis or the Virgin is a tree, in whose branches a Dog and an Ibis sit on either side, as we have previously proven from the Astrology of the Egyptians, which Rabbi Avenar <note>Abraham Ibn Ezra, a 12th-century scholar whose astrological works Kircher frequently cites</note> translated into the Hebrew language. The Tree indeed represents the entire substance of vegetable nature, whose presiding deities are the spirits Mercury and Isis, who are aptly denoted by the Dog and the Ibis, as we demonstrated in the *Pamphilian Obelisk*. For when, under the twelfth-part of the Ear-bearing Virgin <note>Spica Virginis</note>—that is, Isis—the abundance of the Nile waters gave great hope for a rich harvest and other plants; lest the seeds of human-sustaining nature, conceived in the earth by her incubation, should be dried up by Typhonian force <note>referring to Typhon/Set, the god of chaos and drought</note> through a lack of water, or suffocated by an excess, they consecrated these Mercurial spirits as sentinels to this sign, whose vigilance and care for the rising of the Nile would provide the Egyptian land with the desired benefit against adverse powers.

**XIII.** The *Iconism* placed within the Rhombus of <term>Omphtæ</term> or the Scales <note>Libra</note> displays the deity <term>Ammon</term> <note>original: "Αμμῶν"</note> transformed with a bull's head, over which hangs a beam in the shape of a plow, as we proved above from Avenar. By these is marked the station of the presiding spirits of spermatic <note>generative/seed-bearing</note> nature, which, under the protection of the deity <term>Omphtæ</term> (who balances all things in equal proportion), was promoted and perfected through the industry of the presiding spirits of agriculture, whose symbols were the Ox and the plow; this occurred after the land was stripped of its Nilotic covering and broke forth into a rich harvest with various sproutings.

**XIV.** The *Iconism* placed under the sign of Typhon—that is, the Scorpion—according to the testimony of Avenar, was an image of a naked human figure, holding a torch in one hand and a sting in the other, and wearing a Raven on its head; this indicated the Genii <note>attendant spirits</note> who follow Typhon. By the nakedness, the earth is indicated as being stripped of its waters; by the sting, the drying power of the rays, which threatens the destruction of vegetable nature by the withdrawal of necessary moisture, which they also hint at by the torch; by the Raven, however—an animal that feeds on corpses and carrion—the contagion of venomous animals born from the putrefaction of the earth at this time is aptly denoted; all of which are the effects of Typhon and his followers. See the *Pamphilian Obelisk*.

**XV.** The *Iconism* placed under the sign of Arueris or the Archer <note>Sagittarius</note> is an image in human form, notable for a tripartite headdress, which is seen slaying a goat by its horns. By this they indicate nothing other than the station of the spirits of the Typhonian phalanx, the <term>antitychon</term> <note>original: "ἀντιτύχων"; likely referring to opposing or adversarial spirits</note>, whose

care is taken that the horns of the young goat are pruned—that is, by taming the scorching power of the Solar rays—to cherish and sustain the Typhonian fertility <note>Kircher often uses "Typhonian" to refer to the raw, chaotic, or subterranean forces of nature</note>, with the seed enclosed in the bowels of the earth, in order to produce a new offspring of vegetable nature; this occurs under this sign, as we have shown above in the interpretation of the Egyptian Zodiac. This image is also found in the Bembine Table <note>The Tabula Bembina or Isiac Table, a famous bronze tablet depicting Egyptian mysteries</note>, as will be seen in its proper place.

XVI. & XVII. The **Iconism** <term>Iconismus: a symbolic image or representation</term>, under the sign of Anubis or Capricorn, displays a standing Cynocephalus <note>A dog-headed baboon associated with Thoth and the moon</note>, who binds Capricorn with a thong. By this it was aptly indicated that, once the fertile nature of Capricorn was bound by Anubis—that is, the power of the Sun being weakened due to its low position—the Moon and its attendant Spirits (which they indicated through the Cynocephalus) rise up and exercise the vicarious power of the Sun, supplying sufficient moisture to cherish and strengthen the seminal substance enclosed in the bowels of the earth. Indeed, the Dog-image XVIII. marks the station of the Sothiac Deities <note>Relating to Sothis, or the star Sirius</note>.

XIX. The Iconism under the Rhombus of Aquarius is established, and it is the image of a Giant man dressed in the Egyptian fashion, conspicuous by a headdress <gloss>shaped like a goat-fire-sphinx</gloss> <note>original Greek: αιγο-πυρο-σφιμὀρφῳ</note>, because he holds a club in his right hand and the scepter of Momphta in his left: through the Giant body and the club, he signifies strength over earthly things; through the multiform headdress, the power which he holds over the air, fire, earth, and the life of things; through the Momphtaean scepter, he denotes dominion over the substance of moist nature. This power he exerts in the Canopic Kingdom while he cherishes, solidifies, strengthens, subdues, and animates the seed enclosed in the earth by rains and snows for the conceiving of various offspring. And this is the station which the Egyptians called the "shutting of Osiris into the ark," as was proved in Treatise II from Plutarch, where we also interpreted the symbolic allusions at length.

XX. The Iconism is placed under the **Rhombus of Ichthon** <term>Ichthon: an Egyptian name used by Kircher for the sign of Pisces</term>, and it is a female figure, which appears in the **Bembine Table** conspicuous with a veil, sitting, and with swelling breasts, bearing in one hand a Lotus-shaped scepter and in the other a Handled Cross <note>The Ankh</note>, whose thigh is also adorned with the same Tautic characters <note>Symbols related to the god Thoth or the letter Tau</note>: by the female figure, with swelling breasts and conspicuous veil, they noted the station of the fertile Deities, with the seeds of the things of the World still covered under the earth, but with the earth now imbued with the spirit of the Sun, breaking out into open germination; which is aptly suggested by the Lotus-bearing scepter, and shown by the Handled Crosses with which the thigh is marked, by which the various mixtures of feminine principles, struck by the darts of the Solar rays, break forth into the fertile generation of all things; which happens under this Rhombus of Ichthon, or the station of Pisces: for Ichthon, through his attendants of hidden things, according to the testimony of **Iamblichus**, leads the reason of things out of the darkness under which they lay into the light, so that those things which the Deities of the preceding sign had hidden away closed in the earth, he may lead into open and fertile progeny as the earth is gradually opened—that is, as the Sun gradually rises and strikes the earth more powerfully with its rays.

We have seen the mystical significations of the Northern Constellations; it remains that we open the secrets of the Southern ones with equal pace.

**Iconism XXI.** In the Southern Realm of Osiris, beneath the Rhombus of Ammon (or the first position of Aries), there appears a serpent coiled around a staff. This indicates the station of the <term>Agathodaemons</term> <note>From the Greek for "Good Spirits," often depicted as winged serpents or protective deities</note>, the presiding guardians of the life of things. These spirits, having entered through the Nilotic Delta—that is, the "Gate of the Gods," as we explained above—awaken all things to life under the protection of Ammon. At the proper time, they arrange the beneficial moisture in the furthest reaches of the South, which is aptly suggested by the overflowing streams of the Nile shown in Iconism XIX.

**Iconism XXII.** Beneath the sign of Apis in the South, they place the image of <term>Pan</term> <note>Kircher identifies the Greek Pan with the Egyptian Min or Mendes, gods of fertility and wild nature</note>, which represents the station of the Panic Deities. Under their protection, all things conspire toward the fertile production of life, which occurs during this season.

**Iconisms XXIII. & XXIV.** Positioned beneath the signs of Gemini and Cancer, these exhibit a <term>Serpent-bearer</term> with a lance, above whom floats a ship distinguished by the heads of rams; in the middle of the ship stands a Bull, or <term>Apis</term>. Through the lanced Serpent-bearer, the station of the <term>Arimanian Powers</term> <note>A reference to Ahriman, the destructive spirit in Zoroastrianism, used here to represent scorching, drying forces</note> is indicated, by which the moisturizing power of the solar rays is destroyed by a parching force. Here is placed Apis carried in a ship—that is, <term>Oromasdes</term> <note>Ahura Mazda, the principle of light/good; Kircher views the Egyptian gods through the lens of "Ancient Theology" linking Persia, Greece, and Egypt</note>. The Sun, carried over the Southern region as if through moisture, attracts new moisture from rivers, lakes, and seas by the attractive force of its rays. Once these are resolved into rains, the new preludes to the rising of the Nile are prepared.

**Iconisms XXV. & XXVI.** Positioned beneath the Rhombus of Cancer and Leo, <term>Anubis</term> is shown transfixing a wolf or a Typhonian beast. By this, they wished to indicate the station of the Mercurial or Nilotic Deities, whose care it is to accelerate the rising of the Nile at this time. This occurs during the rising of the <term>Dog Star</term>, which in Egyptian is called <term>Sothis</term> <gloss>or Sothis</gloss> <note>original: "ⲥⲱⲑ seu Sothis"</note>. We have shown in the *Pamphilian Obelisk* that Mercury was also called by this name. At this time, the earthy and parching power of Typhon—indicated not incongruously by the Wolf, a terrestrial and fierce animal into which Typhon is said to have transformed himself—is destroyed by the exuberance of the Nilotic moisture.

**Iconisms XXVII. XXVIII. XXIX. XXX.** These are positioned beneath the signs of Virgo and Libra. First is the <term>Giant</term> <note>original: "Γύγας" (Gygas)</note>, whom the Greeks call Orion; he is joined by an Owl and a Quail, according to the witness of <term>Avenar</term> <note>Abraham Ibn Ezra, a medieval Jewish scholar and astrologer</note>, and these are symbols of ill omen. Through the Giant, an inauspicious Titanic station is foretold—that is, of Genii who suffocate all things by an excess of moisture. Opposed to their tyranny is a Lion carried in a ship—that is, <term>Momphta</term> and <term>Omphta</term> <note>Kircher's names for Egyptian demiurges or aspects of divine power</note>. The former, with his followers, blesses the earth with sufficient moisture; the latter busies himself with tempering the excess of suffocating moisture brought on immoderately by the Titanic power, reducing it to a healthy medium. See what we have discussed copiously on these matters in the interpretation of the Bembine Tablet. <margin>Southern Iconisms.</margin>

**Iconism XXXI.** Positioned beneath the southern Rhombus of Scorpio, this exhibits a Crocodile, an argument for the Typhonian tyranny. It is a hostile station because the adverse Genii, who were unable to destroy the good through an excess of moisture, now attempt to accomplish it through a deficiency of the same, as the Nile has now receded within its banks and the dry land increases. It is called the station of <term>Suchus</term>, that is, the Crocodile, into which the Egyptians report Typhon was transformed.

# CLASS VII. HIEROGLYPHIC MATHEMATICS. CHAPTER XII

**Images XXXII & XXXIII**, located within the southern rhombs <note>rhombus: a diamond-shaped geometric division of the celestial sphere</note> of Sagittarius and Capricorn, contain the likeness of a human figure piercing a Hippopotamus with one hand, while the other hand holds an Ibis that is devouring a Serpent. By the man in youthful dress distinguished by a headband, **Horus** is understood; by the Hippopotamus, **Typhon** <note>In Kircher’s system, Horus represents the restorative power of nature, while Typhon represents destructive chaos or drought</note> is meant. Indeed, Horus is the symbol of the reborn World, by whom the contagious power of the remaining moisture is transfixed. These things are also indicated by the Ibis, the symbol of the **Mercurial Spirits** <note>Genii: intermediary spirits or presiding deities</note>, by whose help the swarming multitude of harmful things born from the putrefaction of the earth is consumed at this time.

**Images XXXIV, XXXV, & XXXVI**, contained under the southern rhomb of Aquarius and Pisces, are the **Nile**, the **Hydra**, and the **High Altar**. By these, the stations of the three Nilotic Spirits—guardians of the southern waters and preservers of the fiery nature—are expressed. The first activate the moisture enclosed in the bowels of the earth; the second make the same fertile; the third administer the subterranean heat by which things are fertilized. These concepts are aptly expressed through the Nile, the Hydra, and the Altar equipped with fire. But regarding these matters, a copious amount of material for discussion will be given in due time in the interpretation of the **Barberini Obelisk**.

Note, Reader, that from the above-cited **Michael Schatta**, only the figures themselves were sent, and those quite imperfectly; nevertheless, as much as I could gather from his letters written to me in Arabic, I have restored them to the correct Egyptian mind and divided them into certain stations of the Gods, so that the intention of the Egyptians in establishing them might appear more clearly. But all these things, as I said, will be better revealed in the interpretation of the Barberini Obelisk.

<margin>
The impious superstition and divination of the Egyptians and Chaldeans derived from the images of the 48 stars.
</margin>

You have, therefore, the arrangement of the 48 Images placed in the sky by the Egyptians, and their physical interpretations. They also adapted these according to a certain analogy to archetypal and moral principles; so that through the said symbols of the Images, the **Intellectual World** might be understood. In this world, they subtly suggested the duties distributed to each choir of Spirits, and the effects they imprint both in the triple series of Worlds and, most importantly, in the spheres of souls; for from here they deduced the order of fates. From the ascendants of these Images of Spirits, they believed they could know an infallible conjecture regarding the fortune or fate of anyone born. Hence, they strove to appease each of the said stations of the Gods with sacrifices, rites, and ceremonies as soon as they emerged from the Horizon or culminated in their ascent. For just as they believed all misery and calamity of the newborn depended on the adverse ascent of Spirits, so from the benevolent and propitious ascent of the <term>Agathodaemons</term> <note>original: "Agathodæmonum" — from Greek 'agathos' (good) and 'daimon' (spirit); benevolent guardian spirits</note> they promised themselves fortune and happiness. Hence, they strove to appease the former with sacrifices so they would not harm, and to attract the latter with appropriate things and sacrifices so they would be of benefit. Since, however, the seven principal Deities of the planets are continually joined—now good with good, now good with malignant, and then malignant with malignant—they pronounced judgments on prosperous or adverse events according to the ratio of the prosperous or adverse conjunction. See what we have discussed more extensively above in Chapters 3, 4, and 5.

This entire collection of Star-clusters <note>original: "Asterismorum"</note> possessed four principal Deities, by whose influential power both the series of linked Spirits <note>original: "Geniorum," referring to intermediary beings or guardian spirits</note> and the management of the lower World are governed. -># DIGRESSION.<-

->### *Whether the Heaven is a certain Book; and whether the various combinations of stars compose a kind of writing, in which future events may be read, inscribed by the finger of God.*<-

<margin>The Hebrews and Arabs assert that heaven is a book in which the future may be read.</margin>
I find that the Hebrews and Arabs were the first assertors of this dogma. For when they beheld the Heaven marked by the Egyptians and Greeks with such wondrous and unusual images of false Deities, driven both by the impropriety of the thing and by the prohibition of the Law, they fashioned another dogma constituted from celestial characters. For these people—partly because they believed fatal laws were described in heaven, and partly because they were deceived by the testimonies of the most ancient Authors—judged it to be by no means vain or idle that the heaven exerted itself upon the lower World with such unusual effects. They arrived at the opinion that the expanse of the firmament is nothing other than a certain book marked with stars as if with certain letters, from whose harmonious combination the events of all ages and the decrees of men might be read, inscribed by the finger of God. But so that they may more skillfully defend this foolish fabrication, they prove it from sacred texts, which they ridiculously distort to stabilize their own whims, depraving them in marvelous ways against reason. They first allege that passage from Isaiah 34:
->**And the heavens shall be rolled up like a scroll:**<- <note>original Hebrew: ונגלו כספר השמים</note>
<margin>The foolish interpretation of Scripture by Hebrew Astrologers.</margin>
*And the heavens shall be folded together like a book.* Which they explain thus: *And the heavens shall be folded together like a book, displaying the accounts of all present, past, and future events.* They confirm this passage from the first verse of Genesis:
->**In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth:**<- <note>original Hebrew: בראשית ברא אלהים את השמים ואת הארץ</note>
Which words they wrongly interpret in this manner: *In the beginning God created the letters or the writing of heaven;* where they explain the particle **את** <note>The Hebrew direct object marker 'et', composed of the first and last letters of the alphabet, Aleph and Tav.</note> as the "letters" or "writing" of heaven. This is an entirely incongruous exposition, deceitfully twisted to persuade the unskilled of that superstitious celestial writing. For who among the Commentators of Holy Scripture has ever interpreted this particle as anything other than the accusative case marker? Which also becomes manifest...

He dismisses the idea that the Hebrew particle 'et' refers to the alphabet rather than a grammatical marker.</summary>

# CHAPTER VII
## THE GYMNASIUM OF EGYPTIAN HIEROGLYPHS
### PAGE 216

This arises from the following word: *and the earth* <note>original Hebrew: ואת הארץ</note> (which, however, those who are studiously aware of their poor cause craftily keep silent), where the same particle is repeated; in place of which the Chaldean paraphrase <note>The Targum, an Aramaic translation/interpretation of the Hebrew Bible</note> has *Iath* <note>original: ית</note>, a particle commonly used by the Chaldeans to form the accusative case. According to the opinion of these people, therefore, the first verse of Genesis ought to be read thus: *In the beginning God created the letter of heaven and the letter of the earth*; an interpretation than which nothing more foolish or inept can be imagined. In a similar fashion, they read that passage of the same Genesis, *and they shall be for signs* <note>original Hebrew: והיו לאתת</note>, as *and they shall be for letters*, by a completely reckless daring. Nor do they stop here; to finally achieve their intent, they take that passage from Psalm 19 <note>Kircher cites it as Psalm 17 following the Vulgate numbering</note>, *Their sound has gone out into all the earth*; they interpret the word *Kolam* <note>original: קלם, "their voice"</note> as *Kauam* <note>original: קום, "their line"</note>, meaning their line—that is, the lines of scripture. This is an equally wretched and clumsy exposition, no better than the first.

<margin>
Authors of the impious opinion claiming that heaven is a book in which future events are described by the finger of God.
</margin>

Therefore, having laid these worm-eaten foundations, they say that the heaven or <term>Rakia</term> <note>The Hebrew term for the "firmament" or expanse created on the second day of Genesis</note>—that expanse, I say—is like a certain parchment skin, in which the stars exhibit letters, and the constellations exhibit words of future events inscribed by the finger of God, according to that saying: *The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands.* In this, they say, all the successes of future things, the mutations of kingdoms and empires, as well as the entire lot and fortune of private men, are set forth as if through a certain book intelligible only to the Wise. And they say the propagators of this opinion were first [Simeon bar] Yochai, which he explains in the <term>Zohar</term> <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note>, Akiva the author of the book <term>Yetzirah</term> <note>The "Book of Formation," an early Kabbalistic text on the Hebrew alphabet</note>, Rambam <note>Maimonides</note>, Abraham Dior, Ibn Ezra, Radak, Yom Tov, Ralbag, Abarbanel, and countless others. Some Latin writers, more superstitious than the rest, have followed them and contend to stabilize their dogma from a certain apocryphal book entitled the *Narration of Joseph*, which they assert Origen cites in his book *Whether the Stars Act*; in which these words are held: *I read in the tablets of heaven what will happen to you and your sons.* To this they also twist that passage of St. Augustine in Book 2 *Against the Manichaeans*, chapter 21: *Nor is it to be believed that thoughts can lie hidden in those celestial bodies in the same way they lie hidden in these [human] bodies; but just as certain movements of the mind appear in the face, and especially in the eyes, so in that transparency and simplicity of the celestial bodies I do not think any movements of the mind are hidden at all.* Yet there, no mention is made of celestial scripture; rather, the Holy Doctor only establishes a certain comparison of the celestial face to the human face. Nor does that line of Orpheus support them: *Your certain order runs in the stars by immutable commands, favoring them* <note>original Greek: Σὺ μὲν ἐν ἄστροις τάξις ἀπελλάντοισιν ἐφημοσύνῃσι τρέχεις</note>. For while they drag this quote here, they are clearly proven vain; since anyone who weighs the context of the Orphic hymns more scrupulously will find that the discourse there is not about celestial scripture, nor about the character-shapes of letters with which they disfigure the heaven, but about the immutable necessity of nature shining forth most greatly in the heavens.

<margin>
Cornelius Agrippa. Paracelsus. Robert Fludd.
</margin>

Among others, however, Cornelius Agrippa explains this opinion at length in his *Occult Philosophy*; Paracelsus in his *Archidoxes*; and Robert Fludd <note>Latinized as "de Fluctibus"</note>, who in a certain apology for the defense of the Rosicrucian state <note>The Rosicrucians, a secret society of mystics</note>, says thus: *Characters of this kind are inserted and impressed in the heaven, which are composed from the orders of the stars no differently than geometric lines and common letters are formed from points.*

He dismisses the claims of occultists like Agrippa and Fludd, arguing that celestial order reflects natural law rather than a literal alphabet of fate.</summary>

# CHAPTER VII. 220 EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

<margin>The Celestial Alphabet is vain and useless.</margin> These letters of the Alphabet are applied to the constellations of both hemispheres in such a way that individual constellations, constructed from said letters, might show something—either good or evil—to one skilled in reading these characters. I have decided to include both characteristic hemispheres in this place so that the Reader might recognize, as if from a prototype, how much human curiosity entangles itself in useless effort with trifles, by exhibiting a business so slippery, utterly arbitrary, and resting on no foundation. For it is so uncertain, disjointed, and <term>disordered</term> <note>original Greek: ἀτακτον (ataktos), meaning chaotic or without arrangement</note> that even though I began a comparison of these characters with astronomical constellations with the greatest zeal and industry, I could not find even one that referred to the commonly known constellations, even by conjecture. Therefore, I judged it a useless and fanatical invention to be utterly rejected. Furthermore, to properly perform the reading of this "scripture," difficulties of immense proportions arise, which seem impossible to overcome by any reasoning. For if a reading is to be established,

<margin>Objection 1 against the Celestial Alphabet.</margin> I ask: where should the first beginning of the reading be made? For besides the fact that the characteristic constellations are always and everywhere the same and immutable, they also exist in common for every place and horizon from which they can be seen; and therefore, one might perceive good in one place and evil in another from them with an equal gaze. Who, then, will interpose himself as a fair judge and definer in a business so slippery? Since it can in no way be defined why good or evil should be portended to this region, city, or man rather than that one, or at what time the threatening script

<margin>Gaffarel's Response.</margin> is to be fulfilled. Gaffarel <note>Jacques Gaffarel (1601–1681), a French scholar and astrologer who promoted the idea of the "Celestial Alphabet."</note> responds to this by citing Rabbi Abiudam: >To know how to perfectly understand this celestial writing, one must exactly observe the vertical stars; for those which are directly over a Kingdom ordinarily show what must happen to it.< <note>Kircher provides the original 17th-century French here.</note> That is: *To know the perfect method of this celestial writing, it is necessary to note exactly the stars vertical to any Kingdom; for these ordinarily show whatever ought to happen to it.* But on the contrary; since the stars

<margin>Instance against Gaffarel.</margin> vertical to any region must be considered, and since those same stars are equally vertical to all those who live under the same parallel of latitude, it necessarily follows that everyone surrounding the globe of the earth would obtain the same effect. There is no reason why the <term>neighbors</term> <note>original Greek: periœcis, referring to people living on the same parallel of latitude but in different longitudes</note> under this meridian should be affected rather than those under various other meridians intersecting the same parallel; for the same always immobile and immutable script is vertical to everyone living under the same parallel once in a 24-hour period. Yet experience teaches that these <term>neighbors</term> have a great variety of effects: some are oppressed by wars, famine, and other calamities, while others enjoy the perpetual happiness of peace.

<margin>Gaffarel's Evasion.</margin> Terrified by these arguments, they found this loophole: they say that the stars are indeed always immobile and immutable, and in this sense that celestial script can least be read; but God manifests the truth of future things and coming events to the Wise, partly through the disparate movements of the planets traveling back and forth, and partly through comets and the portents of new stars appearing from time to time. For while these wanderers traverse all the paths of the heavens, they are always joined somewhere with the aforementioned constellations; thus it happens from this meeting, now at the beginning, a little—

### CLASS VII. MATHEMATICAL HIEROGLYPHICS. CHAPTER VII

...placed afterward in the middle, and finally at the end of some notable <term>asterism</term> <note>A recognizable pattern of stars, such as a constellation.</note>, a meaning might be drawn out for those things which they indicate. Gaffarel clarifies the matter with an example; he says that in this French word, *AME* <note>original: "AME," meaning soul</note>, if an *F* is joined to the beginning, you create the word *FAME* <note>original: "FAME," meaning hunger or reputation</note>; if an *R* is joined in the middle, it creates the word *ARME* <note>original: "ARME," meaning weapon</note>, and so on for the rest. He adds that since there are stars of various magnitudes in the constellations, the larger ones behave like capital letters and are more significant, and therefore one must sometimes attend to them alone. Thus (he says), if in this word, *EMPEREUR* <note>original: "EMPEREUR," meaning Emperor</note>, I want to read the word *PERE* <note>original: "PERE," meaning father</note>, I would write *EMPEREUR* thus: emPEREur; and so the capital letters alone mean *PERE*. Similarly, if in the word *ROYAUME* <note>original: "ROYAUME," meaning kingdom</note>, I want to read the word *ROME*, I would write *ROyaumE*. 

But who would not laugh at this childish and most foolish way of philosophizing? For if the planets, comets, and other new phenomena of the stars effect this change of meaning in the celestial scripture, I ask them to show me what letter those solitary stars constitute, since a single star is incapable of forming any letter, but many stars—as they themselves freely admit—are necessary to form a figure. Perhaps they will respond that this happens during great <term>conjunctions</term> <note>When two or more celestial bodies appear close together in the sky.</note>, in which a meeting of planets occurs. But let us suppose they form a square; who could then know whether that square forms an <term>Aleph</term> **א**, or a <term>Beth</term> **ב**, or a <term>He</term> **ה**, or a <term>Cheth</term> **ח**, or a <term>Mem</term> **מ**, or any similar letter of square form? For that square which the planets form with the stars could fit all the said letters, as appears in the following characters: 

<margin>Refutation</margin> 

**מ ח ת ב א** <note>Hebrew letters of square shape: Mem, Cheth, Tav, Beth, Aleph.</note> 

In these, since the mere drawing of the lines alone designates the shapes of the letters, the placement of stars into a square seems useless and entirely idle. The same must be said of the linear letters, which consist of only two stars, as in **ו ז י כ ר** <note>Hebrew letters formed by simple lines: Vav, Zayin, Yod, Kaph, Resh.</note>; and in the triangular letters, which are for the most part formed by three stars, such as **ס ל ר ש נ** <note>Hebrew letters with triangular or curved elements: Samekh, Lamed, Resh, Shin, Nun.</note> etc. 

But the supreme vanity of this "scripture" can be seen no better than through examples. Gaffarel brings forward the following examples from Rabbi Chomer: first, the head of Medusa, whose five principal and vertical stars portended the ultimate desolation of Greece, while they formed this Hebrew word **חרב**, *Charab*, that is, *desolated* <note>original: "Charab," which can mean dried up, desolate, or sword.</note>. 

Truly, anyone who examines these things more carefully will find nothing but open deception hidden beneath them; which we demonstrate thus. The five principal stars are designated by five white dots imprinted on the letters; where the first letter **ח** (*Cheth*) <margin>The vanity of the Celestial Alphabet is shown through examples.</margin> consists of two stars, the second **ר** (*Resch*) of one, and the third **ב** (*Beth*) likewise consists of two stars. But as is evident from the "Celestial Alphabet," the letters **ו ח צ ל מ** <note>Vav, Cheth, Tsadi, Lamed, Mem.</note> have the exact same stellar placement as the first letter of said word, **ח** (*Cheth*); the second letter **ר** (*Resch*) has the same as **ו** (*Vau*), **ק** (*Koph*), and **ד** (*Daleth*); and finally, the third has the same as the letters **ת נ כ נ ב** <note>Tav, Nun, Kaph, Nun, Beth.</note>. From which it follows that from the said constellation, one could gather not only the word **חרב** (*Charab*), that is, *desolated*, but also all the following words: 

**מת** (*Death*), **סוף** (*End*), **וית** (*Sign*), **צוף** (*Flowing*), **זקן** (*Elder*), **חרץ** (*Determined*), **חרף** (*Winter*), **ערב** (*Evening*), **טוב** (*Good*).

of which the first, <note>טוב - *tov*</note>, means the same as *good*, a sense entirely contrary to the former; the second, <note>ערב - *erev*</note>, is the same as *to pledge, to mix, a raven, or a willow*; the third, <note>חרף - *charaph*</note>, the same as *to reproach or winter*; the fourth, <note>חרד - *charad*</note>, the same as *to move or to be anxious*, etc.; the fifth, <note>זקן - *zaken*</note>, the same as *to grow old or a beard*; the sixth, <note>צוץ - *tsuts*</note>, the same as *to swim, to fly away, or a honeycomb*; the seventh, <note>חלה - *chalah*</note>, the same as *olive or oil*; the eighth, <note>סוף - *soph*</note>, the same as *boundary, end, or to fail*; the ninth, <note>סון - *sun*</note>, means the same as *an experiment*, as will be evident from a Hebrew Lexicon. Since, therefore, one and the same interpretation can be constructed in so many and such various ways, involving meanings that are sometimes good and sometimes evil, who will ever be certain of the truth of the meaning? It is clear, therefore, that the aforementioned scripture is utterly trifling, nor can any reasoning be devised that could satisfy it in any way.

<margin>Objection 2 against the Celestial Alphabet.</margin>
A second difficulty lies in the fact that it cannot be known to which region in particular such misfortunes are portended. But so they do not seem to have said nothing on this point, they turn to <term>Cabalistic</term> <note>Referring to Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism that includes the interpretation of hidden meanings in the Hebrew Bible.</note> devices. From the numbers of a word—for example, <note>חרב - *cherev*, meaning "sword" or "destruction"</note>—with greatest but useless labor, they seek the name of some region containing the same numerical value. For instance, they mention <note>יון - *Iavan*</note>, which is *Greece*; they thus divine that the desolation of Greece is imminent because this word contains the same number as the word <note>חרב - *cherev*</note>, namely 12. But this reasoning, like all others, is the worst kind, ineptly and violently twisted to their purpose. For when they saw they would not achieve their intent, they attributed different numbers to certain letters than what the common school of arithmetic attributes to them. Thus <note>ר - *Resh*</note>, which usually signifies 200, they attribute 2, having rejected the zeros. In a similar deal, <note>י - *Yod*</note>, which signifies 10, they attribute 1, having rejected the zero. But if <note>א - *Aleph*</note> were to occur, which signifies 1, how will they distinguish this from the unity of *Yod*? I see them getting stuck here, unable to respond to anything, except to openly expose themselves as excellent imposters to everyone.

<margin>The vanity and falsehood of the Celestial Alphabet are argued more fully.</margin>
He adduces many similar foolish and insane mental tricks from the Rabbis Chomer, Kapol, and Abiudan. When Nabuzardan, he says, was destroying the temple in Jerusalem, the stars directly above it formed these five letters: <note>נחשתן - *Nechushtan*</note>, which is the same as *to devastate, to cut down*, or to lead to ultimate ruin. They say that the letters of this word, when broken down, produce the same number as the years the temple lasted from its building until that time. Again, before the Jews saw their scepter shaken and found their liberty captive in Babylon, five stars exhibited these mystical letters: <note>נתק - *Natak*</note>, which is the same as *to break, to demolish, or to exterminate*;

# CLASS VII. HIEROGLYPHIC MATHEMATICS. CHAPTER VII.

...they say this word **רוב** <note>original: *rov*, meaning "to strive" or "litigate"</note> constitutes the number 208, which is the same as the number of years this Monarchy lasted, having been established by Cyrus. The end of the Greek Empire was shown in a similar way through four stars that composed the word **פרד** <note>original: *perad*, meaning "to divide"</note>, whose number 208 corresponds to the duration of this Monarchy. Again, the Athenian Monarchy lasted 490 years, a duration shown by three letters from four stars contained under the word **צרר** <note>original: *tsarar*, meaning "to be distressed" or "bound narrow"</note>, which signifies *to be afflicted with narrowness*. Along with these four stars, four others appear arranged in the form of **כב** <note>Kaph and Bet</note>, which they call fatal and mournful letters; but Rabbi Chomer says that by the double *Kaph*, Cecrops and Codrus <note>Legendary first and last kings of Athens</note> are signified, under whom this most powerful Kingdom was both begun and consumed. With such trifles do the minds of idle men delight themselves. Furthermore, they say that the Roman Consulship could not extend its power beyond 501 years, because that fatal volume of the heavens had decreed it so, and not otherwise, through 8 stars that composed this word **ראש** <note>original: *rosh*, meaning "head" or "summit"</note>, which contains the number 501: the length of time, clearly, that the dominion of the Roman Consuls lasted. Again, the Monarchy of Julius Caesar, founded to suppress the Consulship of the Romans, lasted for almost the same number of years, indicated by six stars which composed this word **שבר** <note>original: *shever*, meaning "to break" or "shatter"</note>, which has the number 502. Finally, Rabbi Chomer thinks he has found the approaching end of the Ottoman Empire through the reading of the stars in this manner: today, seven stars are vertical to it and constitute the word **כאה** <note>original: *ka’ah*, meaning "to be disheartened" or "shaken"</note>, which signifies *to be weakened, shattered, and afflicted with great pain*; and indeed, the number of the duration of the said Empire is indicated by the number hidden under the word **כאה**, namely 1025. Therefore, when this year is completed, it is necessary for this dominion and Monarchy to be finished; which ought to happen in 1655. For by subtracting from the current year of Christ 630 years (the time when the Muhammadan faith began after Christ), there remains 1025 years for the duration of the Ottoman Empire.

<margin>CHAPTER VIII.</margin>

We have decided to refute these things more extensively so that the stupidity and insanity of these idle men might become more clearly known. For I do not know what so-called "beautiful" dogma of celestial writing has excited such a longing in the minds of the unskilled, especially at this time, when the more absurd the inventions are, the more plausible they seem to superstitious men, being greedily received as if with both arms. I have judged that no more effective remedy can be applied to these gradually creeping errors than a demonstrative refutation of such insane dogmas; so that, having suppressed the falsehood, truth may finally be restored to its integrity.

# CHAPTER VIII.

## On the Clocks, or Sun-dials, of the Ancients.

<margin>The division of time was also in use among the Ancients: hours</margin>
If it is true, as the Stoic school knew and as we recounted in Book 3, Chapter 2 of the *Great Art of Light and Shadow* <note>Kircher's own 1646 work on optics and gnomonics</note>, that time is the standard and guardian of things—because it is the index and examination of truth, and preserves the memory and duration of deeds for posterity—then certainly those are worthy of no small praise who, binding the laws of time with shadowy chains, have attempted by an ingenious device to arrest the fleeing years, months, days, and hours, making them present as if they were permanent things. Since time is nothing other than the "measure of the first motion according to before and after" <note>original Greek: *metron tēs prōtēs kinēseōs*</note>, as the Philosopher <note>Aristotle</note> testifies; and since this measure is the rule for all human actions, adopted to avoid confusion, certainly Censorinus teaches at length that in ancient ages, while time did not yet consist of the name "hours," it was called by names distinct to daily actions. Thus they called the evening *boulyton* <note>original Greek: "the unyoking of oxen"</note>, just as the Poet <note>Ovid</note> says:

> When Phoebus removed the yokes from his well-deserved horses.

Likewise, when designating the time before noon, they said *plethousēs agoras* <note>original Greek: "the marketplace being full"</note>, since men gathered in the assembly at that time, as Hesiod says: "When they lead the people, judging the truth" <note>original Greek: *hot’ alēthea laon krinontes agousi*</note>. So Homer designates midday: "When the sun had bestridden the middle of heaven" <note>original Greek: *ēmos d’ ēēlios meson ouranon amphibebēkei*</note>. Indeed, as Athenaeus testifies, the Ancients mostly noted the time of daily acts with the word *hōra* <note>Greek for hour or season</note>, such as *hōra deipnou* <note>dinner time</note> or *hōra baltou* <note>likely "bath time," original: *hōra baltou*</note>. Among the Latins, it is also called *tempestas*; you may judge the same of the ancient Hebrews, who divided the day into Morning, Noon, and Evening, which parts they called Hours. They also observed the whole <term>nychthemeron</term> <note>the full 24-hour cycle of day and night</note> divided into four parts (which they called Watches): the first Watch was from Evening; the second from midnight; the third from dawn; the fourth from noon. From this, some conclude that the Ancients lacked the intervals of hours; they are wrong. For I am easily persuaded that the art of <term>Gnomonics</term> <note>the science of sundials and measuring time by shadows</note> and the distribution of hours existed from the beginning...

# CLASS VII. MATHEMATICAL HIEROGLYPHS.
## CHAPTER VIII.

<margin>The most ancient use of hours.</margin> I deeply consider the remarkable skill of the ancients in inventing things. For since we judge those things to be most useful which we cannot do without and which we necessarily use, it is certainly not likely that the first mortals discovered the use of music and the more obscure (and less necessary) intervals of voices, yet neglected the less difficult and more necessary art of **Gnomonics** <note>The art of making and using sundials or "gnomons."</note>. For if, as the Philosopher <note>Aristotle</note> testifies, time is the "number of motion," and thus the measure of our actions, it must be that either the ancients lacked time by which to measure their actions, or they were not unskilled in Gnomonics. Almost everyone refers the knowledge of Astronomy—and even Astrology—to our first parents, Adam and his progeny, as we have seen above and in Class II. But who is unaware that neither of these sciences can stand without Gnomonics? For the partition of time is highly necessary to both. Therefore, the division of the day into certain parts called <term>hours</term> <note>Hebrew: *sha'ot* (שעות)</note> was most ancient; its principles were designated, as it were, by the very senses. In the sacred books, the use of hours is clearly indicated in various places: in Exodus 9, Deuteronomy 28, and Esdras Book 3, Chapter 2. In Job 11, mention is made of a "half hour," and in Chapter 12: 
> They prayed prostrate for three hours. 
Ecclesiasticus 12: 
> One hour will remain with you. 
and Chapter 30: 
> Every work in its hour. 
From these, such an argument is constructed: If the ancients had hours, they also had instruments by which they knew them; therefore, they also cultivated Gnomonics. Such instruments are called **clocks** <note>Latin: *horologia*</note>; therefore [they must have existed]. But more on these things below in this same chapter. Furthermore, the use of **shadow-measuring clocks** <note>Latin: *Horologia Sciatherica*</note> in antiquity is demonstrated by the expression <term>shadow before dinner</term> <note>Greek: *epideipnios skia* (ἐπιδείπνιος σκιά)</note>, used for the hour of the meal; or <term>walls before dinner</term> <note>Greek: *epideipnōn teichōn* (ἐπιδείπνων τειχῶν)</note>, because the hours were distinguished by the marks of individual letters; it is also testified by the phrase <term>by means of letters</term> <note>Greek: *dia grammatōn* (διὰ γραμμάτων)</note> regarding a clock in Athenaeus, concerning which see Section II following.

Herodotus, in Book 2, writes that <term>Geometry came from the Egyptians to the Greeks</term>, but **Gnomonics**, and the division of days into 12 parts, flowed from the Babylonians to the same. His words are: <term>For the Greeks learned the pole, and the gnomon, and the twelve parts of the day from the Babylonians.</term> <note>original Greek: Πόλον μὲν γὰρ, καὶ γνώμονα, καὶ τὰ δυώδεκα μέρεα τῆς ἡμέρης παρὰ Βαβυλωνίων ἔμαθον Ἕλληνες.</note> <margin>What the ancients understood by the name of "Hours."</margin> In this place, although some contend that "hours" should be taken not for the twelve parts of the day, but for the signs assigned to civil business, or for the Solstitial times; we nevertheless think that the hours were truly twelve **equinoctial** and **equal** parts of the day, which they call <term>common</term> <note>Greek: *koinas* (κοινὰς)</note> and popular, of which there are twelve in every day and night. For it is certain that those mathematicians who placed **Horoscopes** or **Heliotropes** <note>Public sundials or solar indicators</note> publicly and in the open did not propose them only for the learned and those skilled in astronomy, but for the common people; these clocks pertained not only to discerning the Solstices by the reckoning of shadows, but to the civil parts of the day and the governing of daily business. For what did it matter to plebeians and citizens to know the exact moment when the Solstices occurred? Even if the use of such observations looked toward the management of certain rustic works, there was no need for such refined subtlety; these things could easily be discerned with a "fatter Minerva" <note>An idiomatic expression meaning "rough common sense."</note>, so that they might estimate the annual turning points from the civil months, as our Petavius <note>Dionysius Petavius (1583–1652), a Jesuit scholar and expert on chronology.</note> prudently noted in his *Ouranological Work*, Book 7, Chapter 7. Who, moreover, would believe that those machines existed for only one day in the year, or for the few [days] on which those turning points fall?

<meta>This page continues Chapter VIII of Kircher’s exploration into the history of timekeeping. Having argued on the previous page that the division of time into hours is as old as humanity itself, Kircher now addresses the specific physical nature of ancient sundials, refuting the idea that they were merely used to mark solstices. <margin>CHAPTER VIII.</margin>

...were they specific to these times? Truly, it would be a fine and public recommendation to have the opportunity to know that a hundred or two hundred days ago the summer solstice occurred, or when it will occur in the future! On the contrary, the timepieces of the Ancients were machines designed to distinguish the twelve parts of the day, which are so named after the sun's revolution that nothing could be more absurd than to say such a great mass of work served only a single moment, or even a single day. 

Nor does it matter that those timepieces were called <term>summer</term> <note>original Greek: *therina* (θερινὰ)</note> or <term>winter</term> <note>original Greek: *cheimerina* (χειμερινά)</note>; for with these terms they did not indicate the time of the summer or winter solstices, but rather pointed out <term>equinoctial timepieces</term>. These devices, placed upon an equinoctial plane, demonstrate the hours with their perpetual <term>gnomon</term> <note>the needle or blade of a sundial that casts the shadow</note> on the upper side when the Sun passes through the summer signs; on the lower side, they show the same hours during the remaining half of the year when the Sun passes through the winter signs, as is well known even to those with a basic knowledge of **Gnomonics** <note>the art of constructing and using sundials</note>. There were, however, various types of timekeeping instruments used by the Ancients: **Gnomonic** (or **Sciatheric** <note>shadow-measuring instruments</note>), **Hydraulic** <note>water clocks</note>, and **Sympathic** <note>clocks supposedly working through "natural sympathy" or magnetic forces</note>. Among the Gnomonic types, there were several varieties. We shall begin our discussion of these individually, starting with the Shadow-measuring (Sciatheric) types.

### § I.

->**On the Shadow-measuring Dial of Ahaz.**<-

Among the most famous timepieces of the Ancients was the **Sundial of Ahaz**, which is recorded for us in these words in chapter 20 of the 4th Book of Kings <note>modern 2 Kings 20:11</note>:

<note>original Hebrew: ויקרא ישעיהו הנביא אל יהוה וישב את הצל במעלות אשר ירדה במעלות אחז אחרנית עשר מעלות׃</note>
> *And Isaiah the prophet cried to the Lord, and the shadow returned by the steps which it had gone down in the dial of Ahaz, ten steps backward.*

Or as Isaiah has it in chapter 38, verse 8:

<note>original Hebrew: הנני משיב את צל המעלות אשר ירדה במעלות אחז בשמש אחרנית עשר מעלות ותשב השמש עשר מעלות במעלות אשר ירדה ׃</note>
> *Behold, I will bring back the shadow of the lines, or steps, by which it had gone down on the dial of Ahaz, ten lines or steps backward in the sun. And the sun returned ten steps by the steps it had gone down.*

Or as the **Chaldean Paraphrase** <note>The Targum, an Aramaic translation and commentary on the Hebrew Bible</note> has it:

<note>original Aramaic: הא אנא מתיב ית טול אבן שעיא דנחתת במסקנא דאחז שמשא לאחורוהי עשר שעין ותב שמשא עשר שעין בצורת אבן שעיא דנחתה ׃</note>
> *Behold, I will make the shadow of the stone of hours return, which the sun had descended through the steps of Ahaz, ten hours backward: and the sun returned ten hours on the form of the stone of hours, by which it had descended.*

The **Septuagint** <note>the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament</note> has it thus: 

<note>original Greek: ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ στρέφω τὴν σκιὰν τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν, οὓς κατέβη ὁ ἥλιος τοὺς δέκα ἀναβαθμοὺς τοῦ οἴκου τοῦ πατρός σου ὁ ἥλιος · ἀπέστρεψε...</note>
> *Behold, I turn the shadow of the steps, by which the sun has gone down the ten steps of the house of your father... the sun turned back...*

### SECTION VII. HIEROGLYPHIC MATHEMATICS. 227 CHAPTER VIII.

"Behold, I will turn back the shadow of the steps which the sun has gone down in the house of your father, by ten steps." <note>Original Greek (Septuagint): ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ στρέφω τὴν σκιὰν τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν οὓς κατέβη ὁ ἥλιος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ πατρός σου δέκα ἀναβαθμούς.</note> *Behold, I turn the shadow of the steps, which the Sun went down ten steps in the house of his father; I will turn back the Sun by the ten steps which the shadow descended.* <note>Original Latin Vulgate paraphrase: Ecce ego verto umbrã graduum, quos descendit decem gradus domus patris sui Sol; auertam Solem decem gradibus, quos descendit vmbra.</note>

We establish, therefore, that this **Sun-dial** was **gnomonic** or **Sciatheric** <note>from the Greek 'skia' for shadow; an instrument that tells time by the shadow of a needle</note>; <margin>The Sun-dial of Ahaz was sciatheric, and marked with hour-lines.</margin> we establish that it was in the house of Ahaz, the father of Hezekiah, King of Judah; and we establish that it was marked with hour-lines. However, what kind of dial it was, and with what system of hours it was marked, remains to be explained.

Some think this Sun-dial was horizontal; they gather this from the **Chaldaic paraphrase** <note>the Aramaic Targum</note>, where it is written: <gloss>Stone of hours</gloss> <note>Original Aramaic: אבן שעיא (Auen Schaia)</note>. Some think it was a **hemicycle**, in the form of a **Scaphium** <note>a bowl-shaped sundial common in antiquity</note>, placed before the King's doors. Most of the Rabbis believe it was on the wall of the Royal house; this is gathered from **Radak** <note>Rabbi David Kimhi, a 12th-century scholar</note> in his exposition of this passage:

<margin>Rabbi Radak</margin> <gloss>And the Sun returned backward, and the shadow was on the first step in the Sun-dial of Ahaz, because he himself had built those steps; and it descended, and that which descended was in the steps of Ahaz.</gloss> <note>Original Hebrew: ושב השמש אחרנית והיה הצל במעלה הראשונה במעלות אחז כי הוא בנה אותם המעלות וירד ואשר ירדה במעלות אחז</note>

*And the Sun returned backward, and the shadow was on the first step in the Sun-dial of Ahaz, because he himself had built the Sun-dial in his house, in which the steps descended.*
Or as **Ralbag** <note>Rabbi Levi ben Gershom, a 14th-century philosopher and astronomer</note> has it:
<margin>Rabbi Ralbag</margin> <gloss>Which Sun-dial Ahaz had built in the Royal house.</gloss> <note>Original Hebrew: שבנה אחז בבית המלכות</note>
*That Sun-dial which Ahaz had built in the Royal house.* That it was indeed **vertical**, and faced directly south, **Rabbi Salmon** <note>Kircher's name for Rashi, the preeminent medieval commentator</note> shows in this place with these words:
<margin>Rabbi Salmon</margin> <gloss>And it was a kind of steps made facing the sun to examine the hours of the day.</gloss> <note>Original Hebrew: והיה כמין מדרגות עשויות כנגד החמה לבחון שעות היום</note>

It was, moreover, a kind of steps which were directed toward the Sun—that is, toward the south—so that the hours of the day might be tested by them. Now, since the sundial was intended for public use and for determining the civil business usually carried out in the Royal house according to specific times, it is likely that it was a large, elegant device. As it was open to all, it was situated in the primary location of the City—that is, the Royal palace—serving both as an ornament and for public utility, as I said, and for the efficient management of business, positioned above the gate of the house. Nor do I see why some Authors want it to have had the form of a **Scaphium hemicycle**; for that, besides being small, could not have served public utility as well, since the hours cannot be seen except by those looking closely into the hollow stone. It remains, therefore, that it was drawn upon a vast and **vertical** (as the **Gnomonists** say) surface of polished marble, <margin>The Sun-dial of Ahaz was vertical, facing directly south.</margin> which faced precisely south. The only doubt occurring here is what kind of hours it was marked with; for it was clear from the Chaldaic Paraphrase cited earlier that it was described with hour-lines. To explain this, it should be noted that four types of hours are generally assigned by Astronomers. The first type consists of 24 hours from sunrise to sunrise, used mostly by the **Babylonians**; <margin>Four types of shadow-measuring sun-dials.</margin> the second counts 24 hours conversely from sunset to sunset, and is especially in use among the **Italians**...

# EGYPTIAN HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

<margin>
CHAPTER
VIII.
</margin>

...is in use; the third method counts 24 hours from noon to noon, as Astronomers are accustomed to do, which is why they are called **Astronomical hours**; or even from midnight to midnight, which the Church is accustomed to use in the celebration of feasts, and it calculates them the same way; the fourth method counts 12 hours from sunrise to sunset, and the same number from sunset to sunrise. In this system, an hour is nothing other than a twelfth portion of both the "artificial day" and the "artificial night." Although these hours are all equal in their division of the day, they are nevertheless **unequal** <note>These are often called "temporal" or "seasonal" hours because their length changes depending on the time of year—longer in summer, shorter in winter.</note> in respect to the different days and nights, which are sometimes longer and sometimes shorter; regarding these, see page 215 of my *Great Art of Light and Shadow*. These are also commonly called "ancient hours" because all of antiquity is found to have always used them; <term>Martial</term> <note>A Roman poet of the 1st century AD known for his epigrams.</note> elegantly describes them in Book 4 of his *Epigrams*. They are also called **Jewish hours**, because the ancient Hebrews used these and no others, as is proven from Holy Scripture. To this our Savior Christ alluded: <term>Are there not twelve hours in the day?</term> <note>Original Latin: "Nonne duodecim horæ diei sunt?" (John 11:9)</note>. To this also the <term>Acts of the Apostles</term> alludes regarding the "third hour" when the Holy Spirit descended upon the Disciples; and as held in the Gospels, the "ninth hour" of Christ's death; the former corresponds to the ninth astronomical hour <note>3:00 PM</note>, the latter to the third astronomical hour <note>9:00 AM</note>. Furthermore, in the <term>Sanhedrin</term> <note>A major tractate of the Talmud dealing with law and history.</note>, that most celebrated Talmudic treatise, mention is made of such hours in a legend where the limbs of **Adam** were produced by God through a singular mystery according to the distribution of the hours: in the **first hour**, that is, from the rising of the Sun, God collected his dust; in the **second hour**, the mass of his body was made; in the **third hour**, his limbs were extended; in the **fourth**, the spirit was infused into him; in the **fifth**, he stood upon his feet; in the **sixth**, or at noon, he gave names to things; in the **seventh**, Eve was joined to him; in the **eighth**, the two of them went up to the bed, and four descended <note>A Rabbinic reference to the birth of Cain and his twin sister.</note>; in the **ninth**, he was forbidden to eat from the tree of knowledge; in the **tenth**, other precepts were given to him; in the **eleventh**, he prepared the table; in the **twelfth**, at the setting of the Sun, Adam transgressed.

Therefore, for the Hebrews, there was no other kind of hours than what we have described; from which it follows that the sun-dial of <term>Ahaz</term> was marked with no other kind of hours than **unequal** ones, as was common to all Eastern peoples. From this we gather that the shadow of the said sun-dial, at the time when the prolongation of life was promised to Hezekiah by the Prophet, showed the **tenth hour**, but by a supreme miracle the shadow moved backward to the beginning of the **first hour**, as we have proven above from <term>Radak</term> <note>Rabbi David Kimhi, a medieval biblical commentator.</note>. This certainly could not happen except by the course of the Sun being turned back toward the sunrise by a stupendous miracle. This was not, as some think, an illusion of the eyes, but a true and real retraction of the Sun from the west toward the east, by which the "natural day" was made ten hours longer than usual across the whole earth. This is also evident from the fact that the **Babylonians**, stunned by this unusual length of the day and having been made certain of the retreat of the Sun on the sun-dial of **Ahaz**, sent men to Hezekiah to examine the reason for this miraculous event, as is held in the cited passage.

It is clear, therefore, from what has been said, that such hours were used at all times not only by the Hebrews, Chaldeans, and Romans, but also by the **Egyptians**. But now order demands that we show more closely the nature of the sun-dials of the Egyptians.

->§ II.<-
